items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think of Kenny Barron, I think of Paul Wess, I think of Chris White, you know? These are people who have been around together for many years, so all of them have a place in my heart.

ctx.x: That’s very good. Are there any other key figures, there’s so many that have affected your life and influenced you, any others that you wanted to say something about?

I talked about Donald Byrd, I talked about Billy Taylor. I mean, I wasn’t so friendly with Louis Armstrong, but I was friendly with him. He knew me and I knew him. I think that there are a number of other musicians that I am friendly with who are dear to me because of our relationship over the years. I think of Kenny Barron, I think of Paul Wess, I think of Chris White, you know? These are people who have been around together for many years, so all of them have a place in my heart. My current bass player, Kenny…
Is that time? Good. I want to talk about the Jazz Musicians Emergency, when did that begin?
